newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Stg/mark to consolidate, eyes 3.0 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Stg/mark to consolidate, eyes 3.0 marks.

text.p: Sterling is set to consolidate on Wednesday and attempt to regain its footing around 3.0 marks after skidding on Tuesday to lows of 2.9735 marks, said chartists.
At 0835 GMT, sterling/mark was trading at 2.9975/85 against 2.9826/36 in late Europe on Tuesday. Cable was trading at $1.6296/07 against $1.6282/92.

Chartists said sterling/mark, which slid from a high of 3.0627 on Monday to a trough of 2.9735 on Tuesday, was likely to pause for breath after its recent gyrations. But it will also attempt to regain its foothold around 3.0-marks, now resistance.
"It is all a matter of wait-and-see. Cable has come off and sterling/mark has got thumped," said Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank.
"We are still bullish on dollar/mark, so for sterling/mark - as long as cable does not fall out of bed - we would be looking for it to get back above 3.0 marks and 3.0020," said Celaya.
Analysts said once this target was attained, much of the pressure would be taken off sterling/mark.
Sterling/mark inched above 3.0 marks in early dealings on Wednesday, but analysts said the 3.0020 barrier will remain a stiff one to scale. Congestion there is rife.
On a stumble, analysts said sterling/mark would remain constructive as long as it managed to hold above support at 2.9840/60 and 2.9800 marks.
Below that, analysts said a long-term upward trendline, dating from around July 1996 and cutting in around 2.8400 marks, would provide hefty support.

Cable on Wednesday was also poised to recover after it slid to lows of $1.6230 on Tuesday. "For cable, $1.6250/40 is very good support. As long as it hold there, cable should get back above $1.6330 resistance," said Celaya.
